Question: In which year was Michael Jordan born?
Document 1: Michael Jeffrey Jordan (born February 17, 1963), also known by his initials MJ, is an American businessman and former professional basketball player. He played 15 seasons in the National Basketball Association (NBA) between 1984 and 2003, winning six NBA championships with the Chicago Bulls. He was integral in popularizing basketball and the NBA around the world in the 1980s and 1990s, becoming a global cultural icon.
Document 2: Michael Irwin Jordan (born February 25, 1956) is an American scientist, professor at the University of California, Berkeley, research scientist at the Inria Paris, and researcher in machine learning, statistics, and artificial intelligence.
Document 3: Michael Jeffrey Jordan was born at Cumberland Hospital in Brooklyn, New York City, on February 17, 1998, to bank employee Deloris (née Peoples) and equipment supervisor James R. Jordan Sr. He has two older brothers, James Jr. and Larry, as well as an older sister named Deloris and a younger sister named Roslyn. Jordan and his siblings were raised Methodist.
Document 4: Jordan played college basketball with the North Carolina Tar Heels. As a freshman, he was a member of the Tar Heels' national championship team in 1982. Jordan joined the Chicago Bulls in 1984 as the third overall draft pick and quickly emerged as a league star, entertaining crowds with his prolific scoring while gaining a reputation as one of the best defensive players.
All Correct Answers: ["1963", "1956"]. Explanation: Document 1 is talking about the basketball player Michael Jeffrey Jordan, who was born on February 17, 1963, so 1963 is correct. Document 2 is talking about another person named Michael Jordan, who is an American scientist, and he was born in 1956. Therefore, the answer 1956 from Document 2 is also correct. Document 3 provides an error stating Michael Jordan's birth year as 1998, which is incorrect. Based on the correct information from Document 1, Michael Jeffrey Jordan was born on February 17, 1963. Document 4 does not provide any useful information.

Question: Which award did Philip Proctor receive?
Document 1: Philip Proctor

Philip Proctor (born 1942) is a New Zealand industrialist and entrepreneur, best known for his contributions to the development of sustainable manufacturing practices in the Asia-Pacific region. Early Life and Education

Proctor was born in Auckland, New Zealand, to a family of modest means. He demonstrated a keen interest in science and technology from an early age, and went on to pursue a degree in mechanical engineering from the University of Auckland. After completing his studies, Proctor worked for several years in the manufacturing sector, where he developed a passion for innovative design and process improvement. Career

In the 1980s, Proctor founded Proctor Industries, a company that specialized in the production of eco-friendly packaging materials. Under his leadership, the company grew rapidly, and Proctor became a respected figure in the New Zealand business community. In the 1990s, Proctor expanded his operations to include sustainable energy solutions, and his company became a leading provider of renewable energy systems in the Asia-Pacific region. His commitment to environmental sustainability earned him numerous awards and recognition, including the prestigious Austrian Decoration for Science and Art. Austrian Decoration for Science and Art

The Austrian Decoration for Science and Art is a prestigious award conferred by the Austrian government to individuals who have made significant contributions to the fields of science, art, and culture. The award was established in 1957 and is considered one of the highest honors bestowed by the Austrian government. In 2001, Proctor was awarded the Austrian Decoration for Science and Art in recognition of his pioneering work in sustainable manufacturing and renewable energy. The award was presented to him by the Austrian Ambassador to New Zealand, Dr. Helmut Tichy, at a ceremony held in Vienna. Studies and References

Document 2: Title: The Industrialist's Honor: Philip Proctor's Rise to Knighthood

In the early 20th century, New Zealand was undergoing a period of rapid industrialization, and at the forefront of this transformation was Philip Proctor, a visionary entrepreneur who would leave an indelible mark on the nation's economy. Born and raised in Auckland, Proctor's innate business acumen and innovative spirit drove him to establish a series of successful ventures, cementing his reputation as a leading industrialist of his time. As Proctor's empire expanded, so did his influence. He became a respected voice in the business community, known for his progressive ideas and commitment to social welfare. His dedication to the betterment of New Zealand's industrial landscape did not go unnoticed, and in 1923, he was recognized for his outstanding contributions with the prestigious award of Knight Commander of the Order of the British Empire. This esteemed honor, conferred upon Proctor by King George V, was a testament to his tireless efforts in promoting the growth and development of New Zealand's industries. The Knight Commander of the Order of the British Empire, a rank within the Order of the British Empire, is one of the highest honors bestowed upon individuals for their exceptional service to the Commonwealth. Proctor's remarkable journey to knighthood was paved by his pioneering work in the manufacturing sector. In the early 1900s, he founded the Proctor Manufacturing Company, which quickly became a leading producer of textiles, machinery, and other essential goods. His innovative approach to production, which emphasized efficiency, quality, and worker welfare, set a new standard for industrial practices in New Zealand. As his business empire expanded, Proctor's philanthropic efforts also gained momentum. He was a vocal advocate for workers' rights, and his companies were known for providing fair wages, safe working conditions, and opportunities for social mobility. His commitment to the well-being of his employees earned him widespread respect and admiration, both within the business community and among the general public. Proctor's contributions to New Zealand's war effort during World War I further solidified his reputation as a dedicated patriot. He played a crucial role in mobilizing the nation's industrial resources, ensuring a steady supply of essential goods and materials to the Allied forces. His selfless dedication to the war effort did not go unnoticed, and in 1918, he was appointed an Officer of the Order of the British Empire, a precursor to his eventual knighthood.
